cli.holes: Hole pattern file (fixed G0 holes or own tile, format blindsight.holes or rod positions export)
cli.holes_error: Error in the hole pattern file. {error}
cli.json: JSON output file of the geometry
cli.lang: Language of the output (de, en, fr)
cli.rods: JSON output file of the rod positions per layer
cli.time: Time limit in seconds (overrides the configuration)
config.allowed_empty: stack.allowed_planes. Must not be empty (None = all layers)
config.angle_range: search.angle_max. Must be greater than angle_min
config.angle_step_small: search.angle_step. Too small, gives more than {count} angles
config.axis_outside: motor.axis_height. The output shaft lies outside the motor height
config.border_too_wide: bounds.border_width. The edge strip is wider than half the board
config.bounds_area: bounds. The build area has no positive area (width and height greater than 0)
config.cd_outside: motor.center_distance. The centre distance {cd:g} lies outside the range {lo:g} to {hi:g}
config.cd_together: motor.center_distance_min. Minimum and maximum centre distance must be given together
config.custom_tile_holes: search.custom_tile.holes. At least one hole [x, y] inside the tile is required (0 <= x < width, 0 <= y < height)
config.custom_tile_missing: search.custom_tile. The pattern 'own tile' needs a tile from the hole pattern generator
config.custom_tile_size: search.custom_tile. Width and height must be positive
config.distances_count: stack.distances. Mode 'distances' needs {n} distances to G0
config.distances_order: stack.distances. Distances to G0 must be positive and strictly increasing
config.edge_margin: bounds.edge_margin. Edge margin is larger than half the build area
config.gaps_positive: stack.gaps. All layer distances must be positive
config.holes_format: holes. Every hole must be [x, y] with finite numbers
config.holes_missing: holes. The optimizer 'fixed holes' needs a hole pattern (at least one hole)
config.no_pattern: search.patterns. At least one pattern is required
config.obstacle_size: {tag}. Width and height must be positive
config.outline_convex: motor.outline. Outline must be convex (give non convex motors as their hull)
config.outline_points: motor.outline. At least 3 points [x, y] are required
config.pattern_holes_free: search.pattern. The pattern with individually turned motors has no free pattern, please choose a shape
config.pattern_pitch_missing: search.pattern_pitch. Check fixed distance needs a hole distance
config.plane_key: {label}. Key '{key}' is not a motor layer (1..{n})
config.planes_overlap: stack. Layers G{a} and G{b} overlap. Distance {distance:.2f} mm is smaller than the thickness of G{a} ({thickness:.2f} mm)
config.thicknesses_count: stack.thicknesses. {n} thicknesses expected (one per motor layer)
config.thicknesses_positive: stack.thicknesses. All thicknesses must be positive
config.weights_zero: search.weights. Not all weights may be 0
config.zone_shape: stack.mount_zones[{key}]. Area must be [xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax] with xmax>xmin, ymax>ymin
diagnose.no_plane: No motor layer is usable. Increase the layer distance, choose a lower motor or change the mounting
diagnose.single_fails: Not even a single unit fits into the build area. Most frequent reason. {reason}
diagnose.unit_size: The unit reaches up to {radius:.1f} mm from the rod axis. Build area {width:.0f} by {height:.0f} mm
exhaustive.not_proven: Solution found, but smaller windows were not fully refuted (node limit or cancellation). Not proven optimal.
exhaustive.proven: Window with the fewest grid points on the {step:.2f} mm grid proven (all smaller windows fully refuted, window in the corner of the build area). A smaller arrangement may exist in continuous space or elsewhere.
exhaustive.too_large: The exact mode is only meant for up to {max} rods (target number {target}). Please use 'pattern_greedy' or 'anneal_free'.
field.bounds.border.help: Off means holes and motors must lie fully on the board and may go anywhere. On means a strip of the set width runs along the board edge. Only motors and gears may lie in it, the holes stay in the inner hole area. Nothing reaches beyond the board. How much the motors should use the strip is set with the goals (Small edge or Clean alignment).
field.bounds.border.label: Edge strip for motors only
field.bounds.border.tip: A strip along the board edge that only motors may reach into, the holes stay inside
field.bounds.border_width.label: Width of the edge strip
field.bounds.border_width.tip: Width of the strip along the board edge that only motors may reach into
field.bounds.edge_margin.help: Strip along the board edge where nothing may lie at all, for example for mounting or a housing wall. The holes additionally keep the edge strip for motors when it is switched on.
field.bounds.edge_margin.label: Keep out edge for all parts
field.bounds.edge_margin.tip: Additional distance of all parts to the board edge
field.bounds.height.label: Height (y)
field.bounds.height.tip: Extent of the build area in y from the origin at the bottom left
field.bounds.parts_in_bounds.help: No parts means motors and gears stay on the board. Motors and gears lets them reach beyond the edge as far as needed, only the holes must lie on the board. For a limited overhang use the edge strip for motors.
field.bounds.parts_in_bounds.label: May reach beyond the board edge
field.bounds.parts_in_bounds.tip: Whether motors and gears may reach beyond the board
field.bounds.width.label: Width (x)
field.bounds.width.tip: Extent of the build area in x from the origin at the bottom left
field.clearance.help: Minimum distance in space between all parts of different units (housing, gear, rod) and to obstacles. The true smallest distance of the bodies is measured, not the distance of their centres. Larger values give more room for assembly and manufacturing, but fewer rods.
field.clearance.label: Clearance
field.clearance.tip: Minimum distance between all parts of different units
field.motor.axis_height.help: Height of the output shaft above the mounting face of the motor. It sets the height of the gear and thus where it engages on the rod and whether it fits between the layers.
field.motor.axis_height.label: Shaft height above mounting face
field.motor.axis_height.tip: Height of the output shaft above the mounting face
field.motor.center_distance.help: Distance between gear axis and rod axis. It sets where the motor sits relative to the rod. The gear engages the thread at this distance, no tooth shape is modelled. Please check the real mesh with the real parts. With a motor sketch the value comes from the dimension from the origin to the gear centre.
field.motor.center_distance.label: Gear to rod centre distance
field.motor.center_distance.tip: Distance of the output shaft to the rod axis. The mesh is modelled by this distance only
field.motor.center_distance_max.help: Optional. Upper limit of the variable centre distance, only together with the minimum. The nominal value must lie between min and max.
field.motor.center_distance_max.label: Centre distance max (optional)
field.motor.center_distance_max.tip: Upper limit when the optimizer may vary the centre distance
field.motor.center_distance_min.help: Optional. Together with the maximum the optimizer may choose the centre distance per motor between min and max, for example if the gear can be moved. More freedom can allow more rods but costs computing time.
field.motor.center_distance_min.label: Centre distance min (optional)
field.motor.center_distance_min.tip: Lower limit when the optimizer may vary the centre distance
field.motor.center_distance_steps.help: In how many even steps between min and max the centre distance is tried. 1 means only the nominal value. Every step multiplies the options per motor.
field.motor.center_distance_steps.label: Centre distance steps
field.motor.center_distance_steps.tip: Number of steps between min and max (1 = nominal only)
field.motor.depth.label: Depth (y, shaft direction)
field.motor.gear_diameter.label: Gear diameter
field.motor.gear_diameter.tip: Outer diameter of the drive gear
field.motor.gear_gap.help: Distance between the housing edge where the shaft exits and the gear. With a motor sketch the value is ignored, the housing lies directly in the drawing there.
field.motor.gear_gap.label: Housing to gear gap
field.motor.gear_gap.tip: Axial distance between housing edge and gear
field.motor.gear_width.label: Gear width
field.motor.height.label: Height (z)
field.motor.height.tip: Housing height perpendicular to the layer
field.motor.mount.help: The motor stands on the top face of its layer or hangs below it. This changes into which height range the housing reaches and from which neighbouring layer it must keep its distance.
field.motor.mount.label: Mounting
field.motor.mount.tip: Motor stands on the layer or hangs below it
field.motor.own_clearance.help: Minimum distance of the own housing to the own rod. The mesh of gear and rod is not a collision, but the housing must not touch the rod. Shown as a dashed circle around the rod in the sketch.
field.motor.own_clearance.label: Housing clearance to own rod
field.motor.own_clearance.tip: Minimum distance of the housing to its own rod
field.motor.shaft_x.help: Offset of the output shaft from the centre of the housing, across the shaft. At 0 the shaft is centred. This models motors with a shaft offset to one side. With a motor sketch the value is ignored.
field.motor.shaft_x.label: Output shaft, x offset
field.motor.shaft_x.tip: Lateral offset of the output shaft from the housing centre
field.motor.width.label: Width (x)
field.name.label: Name
field.rod.diameter.label: Diameter
field.rod.engage_above.help: With the rod fully retracted, this much thread must remain above the gear axis. If the gear axis lies too close to G0, the layer check reports a problem.
field.rod.engage_above.label: Thread above gear axis (retracted)
field.rod.engage_above.tip: Minimum thread above the gear axis when fully retracted
field.rod.engage_below.help: With the rod fully extended, this much thread must remain below the gear axis so that the gear still engages safely. Together with the stroke it sets the lower end and thus the length of the rod.
field.rod.engage_below.label: Thread below gear axis (extended)
field.rod.engage_below.tip: Minimum thread below the gear axis when fully extended
field.rod.hole_clearance.help: Play per side between rod and through hole in the boards. Hole diameter = rod diameter plus twice this value. Used for the drill list, DXF and preview.
field.rod.hole_clearance.label: Radial hole clearance
field.rod.hole_clearance.tip: Clearance of the through holes in the layers (per side)
field.rod.length_tolerance.help: Extra length at the lower end of the rod as a reserve, for example for cutting or inaccuracy. It lengthens the rod and thus the range in which it can collide with deeper layers.
field.rod.length_tolerance.label: Length allowance
field.rod.length_tolerance.tip: Additional safety allowance of the rod length
field.rod.retract_depth.help: Where the rod tip lies with the rod fully retracted, measured below the top face of G0. 0 means flush with G0. A larger value moves the whole rod deeper.
field.rod.retract_depth.label: Retracted tip below G0
field.rod.retract_depth.tip: Depth of the rod tip below G0 when fully retracted (0 = flush)
field.rod.stroke.help: How far every rod must be able to extend above the top face of G0. The value is the same for all rods, no matter on which layer their motor sits. Deeper motor layers therefore need longer rods (see the Layers tab).
field.rod.stroke.label: Maximum stroke above G0
field.rod.stroke.tip: Every rod must extend this far above G0, regardless of its motor layer
field.search.allowed_angles.help: Fixed list of permitted motor angles in degrees, for example 0, 90, 180, 270 when motors can only be mounted in certain directions. Replaces angle step, from and to. Per layer it is also possible in the table per motor layer.
field.search.allowed_angles.label: Only these angles (list, empty = raster)
field.search.allowed_angles.tip: Explicit list of permitted motor angles
field.search.angle_max.label: Angle to (degrees, exclusive)
field.search.angle_min.label: Angle from (degrees)
field.search.angle_step.help: In which steps the motors may be rotated about their rod. 15 degrees gives 24 positions. Smaller steps sometimes find denser solutions but need much more computing time.
field.search.angle_step.label: Angle step (degrees)
field.search.angle_step.tip: Raster of the permitted motor angles
field.search.fixed_pitch.help: Instead of searching the grid pitch, exactly this distance of the grid points is used. Leave empty so that the optimizer finds the fitting pitch.
field.search.fixed_pitch.label: Fixed pitch (optional)
field.search.fixed_pitch.tip: Use only this grid pitch instead of searching it
field.search.layout_goal.help: Compact packs the rods as densely as possible in the centre (small footprint). Spread uses the whole build area with distances as large and even as possible.
field.search.layout_goal.label: Layout goal
field.search.layout_goal.tip: compact packs densely (small area), spread distributes evenly over the whole build area
field.search.max_block_holes.help: After how many holes the arrangement of the motors (layer, rotation) repeats at the latest. The program takes the smallest block that works. Larger values allow closer distances but the search takes longer.
field.search.max_block_holes.label: Largest repeat block
field.search.max_block_holes.tip: Repeating pattern. The block after which the motor arrangement repeats holds at most this many holes
field.search.max_candidates.help: Upper limit of checked placements as a second brake next to the time limit. Helpful for reproducible runs on computers of different speed.
field.search.max_candidates.label: Max. candidates
field.search.optimizer.help: Patterns and local search. Square and hexagonal grids followed by refinement, a good default. Free distribution. Irregular, often space saving. Exact on raster. Provably best solution on a raster, only for few rods. Repeating pattern. Regular hole pattern that is easy to drill. Fixed holes. The holes are given (Hole pattern tab), only layer and rotation of the motors are searched.
field.search.optimizer.label: Optimizer
field.search.pattern.help: Shape of the hole pattern. Square, all holes on the grid a. Dice five, square with a centre hole, four neighbours at distance a. Hexagonal, six neighbours at equal distance (densest packing). Staggered rows, every second row shifted by a/2, free row distance. Rectangle, separate distances in x and y. Free, rods per tile as before. Own tile, from the Hole pattern tab.
field.search.pattern.label: Pattern
field.search.pattern.tip: Repeating pattern. Shape of the hole pattern. The program searches the motor arrangement per hole and repeats it
field.search.pattern_fill.label: Fill the whole board
field.search.pattern_fill.tip: Place as many holes as fit on the board instead of the desired number
field.search.pattern_pitch.help: Distance to the nearest hole in mm. Empty means the program searches it. With compact the smallest possible, with spread the largest at which the target count fits into the build area. For an own tile the value is the tile width.
field.search.pattern_pitch.label: Hole distance (optional)
field.search.pattern_pitch.tip: Repeating pattern. Distance to the nearest hole. Empty means automatic (compact smallest, spread largest fitting distance). For an own tile the tile width
field.search.pattern_pitch_y.help: Second distance. For the rectangle the distance in y (empty = equal to a, so a square). For staggered rows the distance of the rows (empty = dense like touching circles, a times 0.866).
field.search.pattern_pitch_y.label: Second distance (optional)
field.search.pattern_pitch_y.tip: Rectangle. Distance in y. Staggered rows. Row distance. Empty means equal to the hole distance (rectangle) or dense like circles (staggered rows)
field.search.pattern_task.help: As dense as possible searches the smallest hole distance at which all motors fit and places the desired number of holes in the middle or fills the whole board. Fixed number spread searches the largest distance at which the desired number of holes fits evenly over the board. Check fixed distance takes your hole distance, fills the board and tells which holes can be served.
field.search.pattern_task.label: Task
field.search.pattern_task.tip: What the program should achieve with the pattern
field.search.patterns.help: Only for patterns and local search. Which grids are tried as starting points. square is a square grid, hex_x and hex_y are hexagonal grids with rows in x or y. Comma separated list.
field.search.patterns.label: Patterns (square, hex_x, hex_y)
field.search.refine_fraction.help: Share of the computing time for the local refinement (simulated annealing) after the grid search. 0.35 means 35 percent. Only for patterns and local search.
field.search.refine_fraction.label: Local search share
field.search.refine_fraction.tip: Time share of the refinement (0 to 0.9)
field.search.seed.label: Seed
field.search.stagnation_s.help: When the target count is reached and the best solution does not improve for this many seconds, the run ends early. Empty means always compute until the time limit.
field.search.stagnation_s.label: Stagnation (s, optional)
field.search.stagnation_s.tip: Stop when the target is reached and nothing improves for this long
field.search.tile_height.help: Pattern free only. Fixed height of the tile. Empty means the smallest fitting height is searched.
field.search.tile_height.label: Tile height (optional)
field.search.tile_height.tip: Pattern free only. Height of the tile in y, empty means search the smallest fitting height
field.search.tile_rods.help: Pattern free only. Number of rods in one tile. The tile with its layers and rotations repeats over the build area. The rods lie on a sub grid of the tile, the distances in x and y are searched separately.
field.search.tile_rods.label: Rods per tile
field.search.tile_rods.tip: Pattern free only. Number of rods in one tile that repeats over the build area (layer and motor angle repeat as well)
field.search.tile_step.help: Raster on which hole distances and tile sizes are searched. 0.5 mm means results like 20.0 or 20.5 mm. Finer gives slightly closer patterns, coarser computes faster and gives rounder dimensions.
field.search.tile_step.label: Pattern raster
field.search.tile_step.tip: Repeating pattern. Raster on which hole distances and tile sizes are searched
field.search.tile_width.help: Pattern free only. Fixed width of the tile. Empty means the smallest fitting width is searched.
field.search.tile_width.label: Tile width (optional)
field.search.tile_width.tip: Pattern free only. Width of the tile in x, empty means search the smallest fitting width
field.search.time_limit_s.help: Longest computing time of a run. More time often gives better results. With stagnation the run ends earlier when nothing improves anymore.
field.search.time_limit_s.label: Time limit (s)
field.search.top_k.help: This many different best arrangements are kept and offered for selection in the results.
field.search.top_k.label: Number of solutions
field.search.top_k.tip: How many best solutions are kept
field.search.weights.alignment.help: Rates how regularly layer and rotation of the motors repeat. Counted are neighbours one to four lattice steps apart along the two main directions of the hole pattern. Directions alternating row by row also count as clean.
field.search.weights.alignment.label: Clean alignment
field.search.weights.alignment.tip: The directions of the motors repeat regularly
field.search.weights.area.help: How important a small footprint (bounding box of all parts) is. High means densely packed.
field.search.weights.area.label: Small footprint
field.search.weights.border.help: Rates how deep the motors reach into the edge strip, relative to its width. Set high, the outer motors turn inwards and the board can become smaller afterwards. Only works with the edge strip switched on.
field.search.weights.border.label: Small edge
field.search.weights.border.tip: Motors reach as little as possible into the edge strip
field.search.weights.count.help: How important it is to reach the desired number of rods. The weights are relative to each other, only their ratio counts.
field.search.weights.count.label: Number of rods
field.search.weights.layers.help: Rates how many motor layers are needed, counted down to the deepest layer in use. One layer less saves a board and height. With 0 percent all layers may be used freely.
field.search.weights.layers.label: Few layers
field.search.weights.layers.tip: Put motors on the upper layers where possible so that fewer boards are needed
field.search.weights.regularity.help: How important an ordered square or hexagonal pattern is, that is a hole pattern that is easy to drill.
field.search.weights.regularity.label: Regular pattern
field.search.weights.regularity.tip: Weight of square or hexagonal order
field.search.weights.uniformity.help: How important equal distances between neighbouring rods are.
field.search.weights.uniformity.label: Even distribution
field.search.workers.help: Starts several independent runs with different random seeds in separate processes and takes the best result. Useful with several processor cores. No effect for exact, repeating pattern and fixed holes.
field.search.workers.label: Parallel runs
field.search.workers.tip: Number of processes for independent seeds (1 = no parallelisation)
field.stack.allowed_planes.help: Only these motor layers may carry motors, empty means all. Edited in the table per motor layer.
field.stack.allowed_planes.label: Allowed motor layers (list, empty = all)
field.stack.allowed_planes.tip: Only these layers may carry motors
field.stack.distances.help: Comma separated list, for every motor layer its distance to the top face of G0, strictly increasing. Example 20, 45, 65.
field.stack.distances.label: Distances to G0 (list)
field.stack.distances.tip: Distance of every motor layer to G0, increasing (mode distances)
field.stack.g0_thickness.help: Thickness of the upper reference board G0 through which all rods extend upwards.
field.stack.g0_thickness.label: G0 thickness
field.stack.g0_thickness.tip: Board thickness of the top reference layer
field.stack.gaps.help: Comma separated list, one distance per motor layer. First value G0 to G1, second G1 to G2 and so on. Example 20, 25, 20.
field.stack.gaps.label: Individual distances (list)
field.stack.mode.help: How the heights of the layers are given. Uniform, all layers at the same distance. Individual distances, list of the distances G0 to G1, G1 to G2 and so on. Distance to G0, for every motor layer its distance to G0.
field.stack.mode.label: Spacing mode
field.stack.mode.tip: How the layer heights are given
field.stack.n_motor_planes.label: Number of motor layers
field.stack.n_motor_planes.tip: Number of layers G1 to Gn, no fixed upper limit
field.stack.thickness.help: Board thickness of the motor layers G1 to Gn. Single layers can get their own thickness in the table per motor layer.
field.stack.thickness.label: Motor layer thickness
field.stack.thickness.tip: Board thickness of the layers G1 to Gn
field.stack.thicknesses.label: Thickness per layer (list, optional)
field.stack.thicknesses.tip: Own thickness for every motor layer, overrides the common thickness
field.stack.uniform_spacing.help: Distance between the top faces of neighbouring layers in uniform mode. Must be larger than the board thickness and leave room for motor and gear.
field.stack.uniform_spacing.label: Uniform layer spacing
field.target_count.help: The optimizer looks for this many rods. It tries to reach the number first and then optimizes area and evenness. If the number does not fit, you get the largest partial solution found with a note. With the optimizer fixed holes the number of holes counts instead.
field.target_count.label: Desired number of rods
field.target_count.tip: This many threaded rods with motors are to be placed
field.tolerance.help: Allowance added to the safety clearance for manufacturing inaccuracy and rounding. The check always uses clearance plus tolerance. Example 1 mm plus 0.05 mm gives an effective distance of 1.05 mm.
field.tolerance.label: Tolerance
field.tolerance.tip: Added to the clearance (manufacturing, rounding). Effective distance = clearance + tolerance
fixed.all_served: All {n} holes are served by motors.
fixed.blocked: Collides in every position with the served holes {holes}
fixed.capacity: The permitted number of motors of the fitting layers is used up
fixed.no_option: No layer, angle or centre distance fits at this position
fixed.note: The hole positions are given. Only layer, motor angle and centre distance per hole were searched.
fixed.partial: {served} of {n} holes served. Not served are
fixed.proven_impossible: The complete search shows that not all {n} holes can be served at the same time.
holes.bad_hole: {path}. A hole needs finite numbers x and y in mm
holes.bad_tile: tile. A tile needs a positive width and height and at least one hole inside the tile
holes.empty: Hole pattern file. Neither holes nor a tile found
holes.not_object: Hole pattern file. JSON object expected
holes.outside: Hole {n} ({x:.2f}, {y:.2f}) lies outside the build area
holes.too_close: Hole {n} is too close to hole {m} ({distance:.2f} mm, at least {required:.2f} mm)
holes.unit: Hole pattern file. Lengths must be given in mm
layout.angle_not_allowed: Motor angle {angle:g} degrees is not allowed on layer G{plane}
layout.capacity_exceeded: Layer G{plane} carries {count} motors, {cap} are allowed
layout.capacity_full: Layer G{plane} already carries the maximum number of motors ({cap})
layout.hits_unit: {part} collides with {other} of unit {unit} (distance {distance:.2f} mm, {gap:.2f} mm required)
layout.pair: Unit {a} ({part_a}) and unit {b} ({part_b}) distance {distance:.2f} mm, {gap:.2f} mm required
model.axis_near_g0: Gear axis is too close to G0. Retracted only {actual:.1f} mm of thread above the axis, {required:.1f} mm required
model.gear_vertical: Gear collides vertically with {other} (distance {distance:.2f} mm, {gap:.2f} mm required)
model.housing_vertical: Motor housing (height {height:.1f} mm) does not fit between the layers. Distance to {other} only {distance:.2f} mm, {gap:.2f} mm required
model.outside_border: {part} lies in the edge strip, holes must lie in the inner hole area
model.outside_zones: Motor lies outside the mounting areas of the layer
model.own_rod: Motor housing touches its own rod (distance {distance:.2f} mm, {required:.2f} mm required). Adjust gear gap or centre distance
model.plane_not_allowed: Layer is not allowed as a motor layer
model.planes_overlap: Layers {upper} and {lower} overlap. Distance {distance:.2f} mm is smaller than the thickness of {upper} ({thickness:.2f} mm)
option.stack.mode.distances: Distance of every layer to G0
pattern.fewer: Only {placed} of {target} holes of the pattern lie validly in the build area.
pattern.fixed_failed: There is no valid motor arrangement with the fixed distance {pitch:.2f} mm.
pattern.none_found: No valid motor arrangement was found for the pattern {pattern}. Try a larger distance, a larger repeat block, more time or a coarser pattern raster.
pattern.not_proven: The hole distance is the smallest found on the pattern raster, not proven to be the smallest.
pattern.smallest_known: Smallest distance found for this pattern {pitch:.2f} mm.
pattern.summary: Pattern {pattern}, hole distance {pitch:.2f} mm. The motor arrangement repeats every {cols} x {rows} cells ({holes} holes, block {width:.2f} x {height:.2f} mm).
pattern_holes.dropped: {n} lattice holes at the edge or at obstacles have no room for a motor and were left out.
pattern_holes.none_found: No hole distance was found for the pattern {pattern} at which all motors fit. More time, a larger board or a smaller number help.
pattern_holes.summary: Pattern {pattern} with hole distance {pitch:.2f} mm, {n} holes, every motor aligned individually.
placement.number: placement.{key} must be a finite number
placement.plane: placement.plane must be an integer from 1 to {n}
polygon.gear_overlap: The gear reaches {depth:.2f} mm into the housing (centre distance {cd:g} mm)
profile.gear_axis: The gear centre must lie on the x axis left of the rod (is at {x:.2f}, {y:.2f})
profile.gear_rectangle: The gear must be an axis parallel rectangle of four lines (do not delete horizontal and vertical)
profile.no_gear: No gear. Draw a gear with the gear tool
profile.no_housing: No housing. Draw at least one area of normal lines, circles or arcs (construction does not count)
result.best_fewer: The best rated arrangement has {best} units. Arrangements with {found} units are among the results, but rank behind it by the weighting of the objectives.
result.no_solution: No valid arrangement was found. Possible causes. Build area too small, safety clearance too large, motors too high or too wide for the layer distances, too few permitted angles or layers.
result.none_found: No solution found. This does not prove that none exists.
result.partial_hint: Only {found} of {target} units could be placed without collisions. A larger build area, more motor layers, a smaller safety clearance, smaller motors or more permitted angles would help. Or more computing time.
result.partial_note: Only {found} of {target} rods can be placed. Best solution found, not proven optimal (upper bound after Oler {bound}).
result.single_infeasible: No valid solution. Not even a single unit can be placed.
result.target_grid: Target number {target} reached. The smallest footprint is only optimal with respect to the examined grid, not in continuous space.
result.target_reached: Target number {target} reached, the number cannot increase further. Footprint, uniformity and regularity are the best values found and not proven optimal.
result.target_reached_goals: All {target} holes served. Layers, edge and alignment are the best values found and not proven optimal.
result.upper_bound: {found} rods reach the theoretical upper bound of the build area.
server.running: Project Blindsight runs at {url}  (stop with Ctrl+C)
server.sketch_required: sketch (object with points and constraints) required
sketch.not_lists: {prefix}. points and constraints must be lists
sketch.point_format: {path}. Must be [x, y] with finite numbers
sketch.same_refs: {path}. An element must not appear twice
sketch.side_angle_range: Angle must lie between 0 and 180 degrees
solver.bad_drag: drag. Expected {{ref, target:[x, y]}} with a valid point or entity
solver.drag_rejected: The dragged position violates constraints. The sketch stays unchanged
solver.redundant: {label} is redundant (already determined by other constraints)
solver.timeout: Time limit exceeded while solving (too many or too complicated constraints)
solver.unsolved: The constraints cannot be satisfied at the same time
status.stagnation: Stopped because the result no longer improved after the target number was reached (stagnation).
status.time_limit: The time limit was reached. More computing time can give better results.
svg.desc: Project Blindsight. Scale 1:1, unit mm. Origin at the bottom left of the build area ({x}, {y}). Geometric result, not a finished PCB layout.
svg.not_convex: The outline is not convex and is replaced by its convex hull.
svg.path_command: Path command {cmd} is not supported (only straight lines M L H V Z). Please convert curves to lines first
svg.polygon_points: Polygon with too few or invalid points
svg.scale_positive: The scale must be a positive number
svg.scale_required: The scale of the SVG is ambiguous (width with unit and viewBox are missing). Please give mm per SVG unit.
svg.shape_count: Expected exactly one outline (rect, polygon, polyline or path), found {n}
svg.transform_ignored: The element has a transform attribute, it is ignored.
svg.viewbox_invalid: viewBox invalid. Please give mm per SVG unit.
svg.viewbox_unreadable: viewBox not readable. Please give mm per SVG unit.
tile.none_found: No valid tile was found. Try a larger tile, more time or a coarser tile raster.
tile.not_multiple: The target number {target} is not a multiple of {rods}. Only whole tiles are placed (at most {lower} rods, next multiple {next}).
tile.not_proven: The tile size is the smallest found on the tile raster, not proven to be the smallest.
tile.summary: Tile with {rods} rods ({rows} x {cols}), {width:.2f} x {height:.2f} mm.
tile.summary_offset: Tile with {rods} rods ({rows} x {cols}, offset rows), {width:.2f} x {height:.2f} mm.
tile.target_too_small: The target number {target} is smaller than the rods per tile ({rods}). Only whole tiles are placed.
value.list_numbers: {path}. All entries must be finite numbers
